title: 从屏幕录制到无障碍视频文档：开发者工作流
author: Saifullah Adenwalla
content:
A short recording can explain an interaction that takes several paragraphs to describe: configuring a dashboard, reproducing a bug, or completing an onboarding flow. But uploading a recording is only the first step.

Developers still need to consider readable interface text, accurate captions, download size, keyboard controls, and what happens when the video cannot load. Those decisions determine whether a demonstration becomes useful documentation.

This tutorial walks through a practical workflow for preparing and publishing a video alongside a web application’s written documentation.

1. Design the demonstration around one task

Start with a specific outcome, such as “Create a test API token and verify the request.” A focused demonstration is easier to follow and update than a tour of every feature.

Before recording, write a short sequence:

  1. State the starting conditions.
  2. Perform the task.
  3. Show the expected result.
  4. Explain a common failure and its recovery.

Use a demonstration account and synthetic data. Check the screen for credentials, customer records, notifications, and browser tabs before capturing it.

For technical tutorials, provide commands and code as selectable text beside the video. Viewers should not have to pause a recording to transcribe a terminal command.

2. Prepare the recording for a documentation page

Capture at a resolution that keeps interface labels readable at the intended display size. A full desktop recording may look clear on your monitor but become difficult to read inside a narrow documentation column.

Zoom into the relevant application area, remove unnecessary pauses, and keep enough context for viewers to understand each action.

VEED is a browser-based video creation and editing platform with tools for screen recording, trimming and cropping clips, adding text, generating subtitles, and cleaning audio. In a developer documentation workflow, these features can help prepare a recorded bug reproduction, onboarding walkthrough, or feature demonstration for publication.

For example, a developer explaining an authentication flow could use veed to edit a recording made with a demonstration account, remove pauses between steps, add a label identifying the test environment, and review generated subtitles against the actual narration. Keep error messages and recovery steps in the final cut: they often contain the most useful information for someone following the tutorial.

Use the editor to prepare the content, then evaluate the exported assets against your website's requirements. Check text readability, caption accuracy, file size, and playback compatibility. Editing a clip and delivering it reliably in a web application require different checks.

Keep an editable source recording. When the application changes, that source makes it easier to replace a segment or produce a revised export.

3. Use native HTML video controls

For a documentation clip, begin with the browser’s built-in player. It avoids the work of implementing an entire control interface.

SitePoint’s guide to embedding video with HTML5 provides background on the basic markup. The example below adds a poster, a caption track, and links that remain available outside the player:

<section aria-labelledby="demo-heading">
  <h2 id="demo-heading">Create a test API token</h2>
  <p>A short walkthrough using a demonstration account.</p>

  <video
    controls
    playsinline
    preload="none"
    width="1280"
    height="720"
    poster="/media/create-token-poster.webp"
  >
    <source
      src="/media/create-token.mp4"
      type="video/mp4"
    >

    <track
      kind="captions"
      src="/media/create-token.en.vtt"
      srclang="en"
      label="English"
      default
    >

    Your browser does not support embedded video.
  </video>

  <p>
    <a href="/docs/create-token-transcript.html">
      Read the transcript and commands
    </a>
    ·
    <a href="/media/create-token.mp4">
      Open the video file
    </a>
  </p>
</section>

Make the player responsive without losing its proportions:

video {
  display: block;
  width: 100%;
  height: auto;
  background: #111;
}

The width and height attributes establish the video’s intrinsic proportions, helping the browser reserve space. The CSS lets it fit a smaller container.

The download and transcript links sit outside the video element because content inside it is not a dependable recovery interface for every playback failure.

4. Make captions a separate, reviewable asset

Captions should include spoken content and relevant sounds. Subtitles generally focus on dialogue or its translation.

For native HTML video, use a WebVTT file:

WEBVTT

00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:04.000
Open Settings, then select API access.

00:00:04.000 --> 00:00:08.000
Choose Create test token and copy the value.

00:00:08.000 --> 00:00:12.000
Run the example request with the test token.

Save this as create-token.en.vtt, matching the track URL. Serve it with the text/vtt content type.

SitePoint’s article on HTML5 video fragments, captions, and dynamic thumbnails introduces text tracks. For current format details, consult MDN’s WebVTT documentation.

When preparing captions in veed, review timestamps, speaker changes, punctuation, and technical names before publishing. An automatically generated caption that changes “npm” into an ordinary word can mislead a beginner.

Keep captions selectable through the player rather than relying only on text burned into the image. A separate track can be updated without re-encoding the video and supports additional languages.

5. Explain meaningful visual information

Captions alone do not convey an action that appears only on screen.

Instead of narrating “click here,” say “select API access in the Settings sidebar.” Describe the important result too: “The response panel displays status 200.”

A useful transcript includes both the spoken explanation and essential visual steps. Where important visual information remains absent from the narration, evaluate whether an audio-described version is needed.

SitePoint’s introduction to accessible audio descriptions explains the purpose of this additional information. Test the delivery method in your supported browsers rather than assuming a descriptions track will provide spoken output everywhere.

6. Choose a loading strategy deliberately

The example uses preload="none" because the video supplements the documentation. It asks the browser to avoid preloading video data, although preload is a hint rather than an absolute guarantee.

A poster still loads separately. Compress it and use an image that communicates what the demonstration covers.

For a video that is the main content, preload="metadata" may be appropriate when showing duration early matters. For a page containing many clips, consider attaching media sources only when a viewer requests a particular clip.

Avoid assuming that a visually small player means a small download. Encoding, duration, resolution, and bitrate determine transfer size. Measure actual requests with the browser’s Network panel. The web.dev guide to lazy-loading video explains additional loading options.

Start with user-initiated playback. A technical demonstration is easier to follow when viewers choose when it begins.

7. Handle playback failures explicitly

A video can fail even when the surrounding documentation page loads correctly. Add a visible status message while keeping the transcript and direct file link available.

Place this message after the video in the earlier example:

<p id="video-status" role="status"></p>

Then add this script after the section:

const video = document.querySelector('video');
const message = document.getElementById('video-status');

function reportMediaError() {
  if (!video.error) return;
  message.textContent =
    'The video could not play. Use the transcript or direct video link below.';
}

video.addEventListener('error', reportMediaError);
video.addEventListener('loadeddata', () => {
  message.textContent = '';
});

// Source selection can fail before a media-element error is available.
video.querySelectorAll('source').forEach(source => {
  source.addEventListener('error', () => {
    message.textContent =
      'The video source could not load. The transcript is available below.';
  });
});

// Handle a media error that happened before listeners were attached.
reportMediaError();

This example assumes one video and one source, matching the earlier markup. If you add alternative encodings, a failure of one source should not be reported as a complete playback failure while another source remains usable. Track fallback outcomes before showing the final message.

The HTMLMediaElement error property exposes a MediaError when one exists. Use its code as diagnostic evidence, alongside network inspection; it does not necessarily identify the underlying cause by itself.

8. Version related media assets together

Treat each published demonstration as a small release. A manifest can keep the video, captions, poster, and transcript associated with the application version they describe:

{
  "id": "create-test-token",
  "appVersion": "2.4",
  "mediaRevision": 3,
  "video": "/media/create-token.r3.mp4",
  "captions": "/media/create-token.r3.en.vtt",
  "poster": "/media/create-token.r3.webp",
  "transcript": "/docs/create-token.r3.html"
}

Changing the asset URL when its contents change makes cache behavior easier to reason about. Upload all referenced assets before publishing the manifest or documentation update, and retain older assets while cached pages may still reference them.

Caption timing belongs to a particular edit. Removing five seconds from the start of a video without updating its captions shifts every subsequent cue. Include caption synchronization in the review whenever the recording changes.

Keep text-based manifests, captions, and transcripts in version control. For large recordings, use media storage suited to their size and your team's workflow.

9. Test the published experience

Validate the final page with its deployed media files:

Check What to verify
Keyboard Playback and caption controls are reachable and operable
Captions Text is accurate, synchronized, and readable
Narrow viewport Interface details remain understandable
Slow connection The page stays usable while media loads
Failed request Transcript and direct file links remain available
Content revision The recording matches the documented application version

Also verify the encoded file in your supported browsers. An MP4 extension identifies a container; playback compatibility depends on the codecs inside it.

If media or captions use a separate origin, check the applicable CORS configuration. Prefer a simple same-origin setup for an initial implementation, and use MDN’s video reference when configuring cross-origin delivery.

Maintain videos like documentation

Store the source recording, final export, captions, transcript, and poster as related assets. Assign an owner and record which application version the demonstration covers.

A useful video page combines a focused demonstration with readable text, verified captions, predictable loading, and working recovery links. Maintaining those parts together gives developers a reference they can watch, search, copy from, and revisit as the application evolves.
aiSummary: 一套全面的开发者工作流，通过整合原生 HTML5 控件、WebVTT 字幕、稳健的错误处理和版本化资源管理，将屏幕录制转化为可访问且易于维护的视频文档。
oneSentenceSummary: 一套全面的开发者工作流，通过整合原生 HTML5 控件、WebVTT 字幕、稳健的错误处理和版本化资源管理，将屏幕录制转化为可访问且易于维护的视频文档。
summary: 本教程指导开发者如何随 Web 应用发布高质量的视频文档。文章强调应将视频视为一等公民的文档资产，而非简单的附件。关键步骤包括设计聚焦于合成数据的演示、优化录屏以适应窄栏阅读，以及利用响应式 CSS 的原生 HTML5 video 元素。文中详述了无障碍最佳实践，例如使用独立的 WebVTT 字幕文件（无需重新编码即可审查和更新），并为仅视觉呈现的信息提供文字转录稿。此外，还涵盖了技术实现策略，如刻意控制加载行为（`preload="none"`）、通过 JavaScript 事件监听器显式处理播放失败，以及基于清单（manifest）的方式将媒体资源与应用版本一同进行版本管理。最后，提供了测试键盘导航、字幕准确性和网络韧性的检查清单。

mainPoints.point: 将视频资源视为版本化的文档组件
mainPoints.explanation: 不要上传零散的文件，而是使用 JSON 清单将视频、字幕、封面图和转录稿链接到特定的应用版本。这确保了缓存一致性，并允许在 UI 变更时同步更新。

mainPoints.point: 优先使用原生 HTML5 控件和外部恢复链接
mainPoints.explanation: 使用内置浏览器播放器以减少维护开销。将转录稿和直接下载链接放置在 `<video>` 元素之外，以确保即使播放器失败或不被支持，这些内容依然可访问。

mainPoints.point: 实施稳健的播放失败处理机制
mainPoints.explanation: JavaScript 应监听视频元素及其源子元素的 `error` 事件。当媒体因网络或编解码器问题无法加载时，显示清晰的状态消息，引导用户查看替代格式（如转录稿）。

mainPoints.point: 分离字幕与硬编码文本以提升可维护性
mainPoints.explanation: 使用 WebVTT 轨道代替硬编码字幕。这样可以在不重新编码视频的情况下独立编辑时间和内容，支持多语言，并改善屏幕阅读器的无障碍体验。

keyQuotes: 一段简短的录屏可以解释需要几个段落才能描述清楚的交互：配置仪表盘、复现 Bug 或完成入门流程。
剪辑片段并在 Web 应用中可靠地交付它，需要不同的检查步骤。
仅有字幕并不能传达那些仅出现在屏幕上的动作。
避免假设视觉上小的播放器意味着小的下载量。
一个有用的视频页面结合了聚焦的演示、易读的文本、经过验证的字幕、可预测的加载行为以及可用的恢复链接。
